newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar takes over Japanese share in steel company.
newsitem.headline: Qatar takes over Japanese share in steel company.

text.p: Qatar on Saturday said it has taken complete control of its steel venture by acquiring 30 percent of the equity held by two Japanese companies.

A decree issued by the Emir, Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa al-Thani, endorsed the Ministry of Finance, Economy and Trade's decision to take over the Japanese shares in Qatar Steel Company (QASCO) and declared the firm a fully state-owned entity.
The ministry took the shares on January 20, but the deal was formalised by the emir's decree only on Saturday.
Sources close to the ministry said Qatar might later offer the newly acquired shares to the public as part of a privatisation programme.

The sources said the government paid $165 million to Japan's Kobe Steel and Tokyo Boeki to take their shares. Kobe Steel's shares in QASCO -- incorporated in 1975 with a paid-up capital of 300 million riyals -- was 20 percent and Tokyo Boeki's 10 percent. The remaining 70 percent was held by the state.
Besides the stakes, the Japanese also held management and marketing contracts with QASCO for more than a decade until the agreements expired in 1990.
